subject: Help: Is my ODE model misspecified, ill-constrained, or is something else wrong?

messages.author: 4b681bcd9d4d425d
messages.subject: Help: Is my ODE model misspecified, ill-constrained, or is something else wrong?
parts:
Hi all,

I built (modified an existing) and am running a SIR infectious disease model in STAN. My problem is that I can't seem to get the inputs working correctly, and so I've produced a very simplified version of the model that displays at least some of the same issues. It requires as data only specifying the number of periods to run, and the list of times. I have been using N_t=20 , t=c(1:20), in RSTAN.

When running, it decides my parameter vector is "1.#INF" (Yes, I'm running windows,) and with iter>2, it then hangs indefinitely while trying to get samples. This happens despite the fact that the actual definition of the parameter is straightforward, and even when I've changed it from lognormal to cauchy, it is still not working.

Of course, I'm probably missing something silly, but I've been stuck for a bit - can anyone help out?

Thanks,
David

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help: Is my ODE model misspecified, ill-constrained, or is something else wrong?
parts:
That’s usually a sign that you’ve reached a stiff region of the system of ODEs,
but I’ve had no problem fitting SIR models in the past.  Your model seems to 
be oddly constructed however, as there are no measured states.  In particular,
the output of the ODE should not on the LHS of any probability statement —
only on the RHS before adding a measurement model for an actual measurement.

I’ve attached a more complicated SIR model that fits no problem as an example.

messages.author: 4b681bcd9d4d425d
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help: Is my ODE model misspecified, ill-constrained, or is something else wrong?
parts:
Hi Michael,

Your model is very helpful, and you shared it with me before; the model this one is abstracted from is based on it. Also, your point about the use of the ODE output on the LHS is correct, and I was not thinking clearly when incorporating that into my simplified model. (Altering it doesn't change the behavior)

Perhaps the stiffness may be because this model has a feedback from the R compartment to the S compartment, unlike your model, but that can be a critical feature of the model - especially if modeling multiple seasons. Also, based on a quick check, eliminating it doesn't seem to help get it to converge it a reasonable amount of time, though there are no error messages now.

I'm still unclear about why a stiff region of the ODE is leading to divide by 0 issues in sampling, but if that's not my problem, I guess I'll need to figure out what to do about the fact that there are stiff regions of the ODE - Do you have any ideas?

Thanks,
David

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help: Is my ODE model misspecified, ill-constrained, or is something else wrong?
parts:
The NaN isn’t just dividing by zero — it can happen for various reasons
depending on the floating point implementation.  

Having an R to S component could add enough feedback to make the
ODEs stiff, but it’s hard to say until you share an updated model that
properly uses measured states.  In particular, if you haven’t measured
any S, I, or R states then there will be nothing to constrain your parameters
and it wouldn’t be surprising if that non identified posterior stretched into
pathological parameters.

Additionally, even with a well-defined model it can be helpful to play
with your initial conditions (say with init=0 or some small value) and
start with a small step size to avoid poor adaptation.

parts:
Hello all,

I am also working on a SIR model and have a similar issue: eternal fitting time. It does not occur for the one-parameter inference, but a real piece of work will involve much higher number of parameters and latent states.
Even I read the discussion above, I am not sure whether I understand what the remedy is. Maybe someone could direct me.

The attached R-file includes the following three steps: 
- generate SIR-data with noise (all parameters are known), extract values of y2 (Infected) to use it as input data for the inference,
- run STAN with one parameter: this works fine,
- same model with two parameters: runs forever.

P.S. you may criticize the way I am creating and fitting noise since these are not two completely consistent procedures: in the fitting part I am not taking into account the cutoff that I am using to generate the noisy values. But I think (and the one-parameter inference supports the statement) it should not be a problem.

Would be grateful for any help and critique,
Liza.

messages.author: f2cad99989ced55e
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help: Is my ODE model misspecified, ill-constrained, or is something else wrong?
parts:
As a note: my issue above was resolved through

- feeding only unknown parameters (subject to inference) into the ODE as theta and other ODE-parameters (but not the parameters of the hierarchical model ) into the system as data x_r, x_i

- changing the step size in the R call through

  fit <- stan(..., control=list(stepsize=0.001, adapt_delta=0.9))

Regards,
Liza

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help: Is my ODE model misspecified, ill-constrained, or is something else wrong?
parts:
Thanks for the update. This has been an ongoing issue for us
with parameters drifting into stiff regions and the simple Runge-Kutta
integrator "locking up" (basically reducing step size until it appears
to just hang).

The good news is that new stiff ODE solver we'll be rolling out in 2.10
should be much more robust. And we've built in limits on the RK integrator.
(And when I say "we", this has mostly been done by Sebastian Weber based
on code originally written by Michael Betancourt.)

- Bob
